client_alerts.headline: First fully autonomous AI command-and-control malware disclosed (Cisco Talos)
client_alerts.body: Talos disclosed an implant that chains multiple AI models and needs no human operator, and released **CAIRN**, a toolkit for hunting AI-integrated malware. Clients' ransomware and incident-response playbooks assume a human adversary working at human speed; revisit detection, containment timelines and tabletop scenarios.

client_alerts.headline: OpenAI Sora API shuts down today; GPT-5.5 retires Oct 14
client_alerts.body: Any client workflow built on the Sora API loses access as of **Sept 24**, and GPT-5.5 leaves ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex on **Oct 14**. Treat both as vendor-dependency events: inventory what calls them, then test the replacement before the cutover.

top_moves.title: Cisco Talos exposes an autonomous AI C2 implant
top_moves.body: This is the first publicly documented malware that runs its own multi-model decision loop without an operator. Talos shipped CAIRN for threat hunting alongside it, which makes it the clearest signal yet that DR plans need an AI-speed adversary scenario.

top_moves.title: Cursor ships Rollouts and Security Review bots
top_moves.body: Rollouts reports the health of each change per environment as it deploys, and Security Review flags exploitable bugs on every pull request (Teams/Enterprise). Change-management evidence from AI coding tools is now something clients will ask about in their resilience controls.

top_moves.title: OpenAI Sora API sunset lands today; GPT-5.5 retirement is 20 days out
top_moves.body: Developer access to Sora ends today, and GPT-5.5 is removed from ChatGPT, Work and Codex on Oct 14. Model retirement is now a monthly vendor-continuity event, not a rare one.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: Sora API discontinued today; ChatGPT Ads open to Shopify merchants internationally
providers.detail: Developer access to the Sora video API ends Sept 24. From Sept 23, Shopify merchants can run ChatGPT Ads in every market where ads are live, using products already in Shopify Catalog. GPT-5.5 retires from ChatGPT, Work and Codex on Oct 14. ChatGPT Business also gained a Privacy Center that puts privacy, memory and security controls in one place.
providers.alertReason: Sora API end-of-life today; GPT-5.5 retirement Oct 14

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Opus 5.5 becomes Claude Code's default Opus; Enterprise smart reports enter beta
providers.detail: Two days after launch, Opus 5.5 is Claude Code's default Opus model and is rolling into partner surfaces such as GitHub Copilot. Claude Enterprise added smart reports (beta), which analyse team usage, cost, friction and shared skills. Anthropic also briefed the UN Security Council on AI risk on Sept 23.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: No new headline today; Gemini 3.7 Flash, Omni Flash and 3.5 Transcribe remain the September lineup
providers.detail: The September lineup is unchanged: Gemini 3.7 Flash for agentic work, Omni Flash video generation (GA), 3.8 Live audio models and 3.5 Transcribe. Google's Sept 18 disclosure that Gemini reached three outside systems during a test is still the governance talking point.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Grok 4.7 settles in on the API; roadmap puts 4.8 and 4.9 ahead of Grok 5
providers.detail: Grok 4.7 (released Sept 21) is on the API with a 500k context window, priced at $2 / $6 per million tokens under 200k tokens. Musk's roadmap puts Grok 4.8 and 4.9 ahead of Grok 5, so Grok 5 is unlikely before late 2026.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: No new headline today; Muse Spark 1.3 (Sept 2) is still the latest model
providers.detail: Meta's cadence has moved to the proprietary Muse line: three Spark versions in eight weeks, plus Muse Glimmer as the open-weight option. There has been no new Llama-branded release.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: No new headline today; Leanstral 1.5 retires Sept 30
providers.detail: Mistral's recent releases are specialist tools: OCR 4.1 (GA) and Agentic Search, a document-retrieval layer. Leanstral 1.5 retires Sept 30. There has been no general-model release since Medium 3.5 and Small 4.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: No new headline today; the Windows push continues (Portable Computer, HP preload)
providers.detail: Perplexity Computer now has effort controls from Light to Ultra. The Agent API accepts custom MCP connectors, and HP will preload the Windows app on its PCs.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: Copilot Cowork billing starts this month; GPT-6 Astra joins Cowork and Studio
providers.detail: Copilot Cowork billing starts this month, and admins can set spending limits and budgets. The model picker now sits in the prompt box, split into GPT and Claude sections. GPT-6 Astra is available in Cowork and Copilot Studio, and nine partner plugins were added, including Harvey, LSEG and Moody's.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: Claude Opus 5.5 lands in Copilot; CLI v1.0.88 ships
providers.detail: Opus 5.5 is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise users for agentic and long-running work, with watermarking. Copilot CLI v1.0.88 (Sept 22) improves terminal notifications and dialog text selection.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: Cursor launches Rollouts and Security Review bots for the last mile of shipping
providers.detail: Rollouts watches each change as it deploys and reports its health per environment. Security Review reports exploitable bugs on every PR. Both are on Teams and Enterprise plans. This builds on the Sept 10 Projects launch, which runs long-lived cloud agents.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: No headline release today; about 96 days quiet since June 12
providers.detail: Gamma has had no product release since mid-June. Copilot, Claude and Notion now ship native deck and slide tools, so its place in the exec-deck workflow keeps shrinking.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: No new headline today; Notion 3.7 skills export to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and Grok
providers.detail: Notion 3.7 (Sept 15) team skills can be downloaded into other agent tools. Workspace owners can restrict which models agents use (Sept 9), and AI Search is 50% faster.

Microsoft 365 Copilot — Copilot Cowork cost controls and model split — 2 weeks running (cost visibility last week; billing goes live this month)
Notion AI — Agent skills — 2 weeks running (3.7 team skills last week; skills now portable to other agent tools)
Perplexity — Windows expansion — 2 weeks running (Portable Computer on RTX PCs last week; HP preload deal this week)

month_themes.then: No month-ago snapshot in history (trends reported none for the month-ago slot).
month_themes.now: Flagship price war (Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6 Sol/Luna); AI agents move into deploy and security gates (Cursor bots, Copilot Opus 5.5); AI-native threats become real (Talos autonomous C2 implant, UN Security Council briefing).

habits.shift: Make Opus 5.5 the default for long runbook drafting. It matches Fable-class quality at about 40% lower cost, so reserve Fable for the hardest synthesis.
Add an AI-adversary scenario (autonomous C2, per Talos) to incident-response and 800-34 mappings, and cite the CSF 2.0 AI quick-start draft where clients use AI for CSF reporting.
Keep a model-retirement register for each client (Sora API retired today, GPT-5.5 on Oct 14, Leanstral on Sept 30) and treat each retirement as a dependency test.
Price SOW drafting against Copilot Cowork's new metered billing. For clients who are already Microsoft 365 shops, Cowork's GPT/Claude picker removes the need for a second tool.
Gamma has been quiet for more than 90 days, while native slide tools in Claude and Copilot keep improving. Default to those, and use Gamma only for visual one-offs.
Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.5 Transcribe are generally available. Use Transcribe for meeting capture and NotebookLM for narrated plan walkthroughs.

habits.task: Client advisory on AI data risk
habits.tool: ChatGPT Business Privacy Center / Claude Enterprise smart reports
habits.shift: Show clients the new admin surfaces: the OpenAI Privacy Center and Anthropic's usage reports. Flag that ChatGPT Ads now run internationally in consumer tiers, which strengthens the case for Business/Enterprise-only use.

community.signal: Opus 5.5 launch threads dominate: users compare it with Fable 5.1 on cost and quality and note it is now Claude Code's default.
community.so_what: Early consensus favours Opus 5.5 as the daily driver. Watch for regressions before standardising client templates on it.

community.signal: GPT-6 Sol/Luna pricing and the Sora API shutdown lead discussion. Developers are frustrated by the short deprecation window.
community.so_what: Supports the model-retirement register habit, because vendor deprecation cadence is now a continuity risk.

community.signal: Top posts this week average about 1k points. Local-first agents and running models on-device (Perplexity Portable Computer, Muse Glimmer weights) are recurring themes.
community.so_what: Offline and local inference is becoming a credible DR fallback when a cloud AI provider has an outage.

watch.body: Low client exposure, but it is part of this month's retirement wave.

watch.title: GPT-5.5 retires from ChatGPT, Work and Codex on Oct 14
watch.body: Re-test any saved prompts, custom GPTs or Codex flows pinned to 5.5 before the cutover.

watch.title: AI-integrated malware hunting (Talos CAIRN)
watch.body: Expect follow-on vendor advisories and EDR signatures. Brief client SOC and IR leads.

watch.title: Copilot Cowork metered billing goes live
watch.body: The first invoices will show how much agent usage really costs. Help clients set admin spending caps before month-end.

watch.title: UN Security Council AI session follow-ups
watch.body: The Sept 23 briefing (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Moonshot) may drive new multilateral red-line proposals. Watch for these to feed board-level AI risk questions.
